newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian investors start preparing for christmas.
newsitem.headline: Belgian investors start preparing for christmas.

text.p: Belgian shares regained some lost ground on Monday after last week's turbulent performance.
Dealers said many investors had already started squaring their end of year accounts and begun preparing for the Christmas holiday.
The Brussels Bel-20 leading share index closed up 0.67 percent or 12.42 at 1,860.19. Volume was thin with only 1.88 billion worth of Belgian shares changing hands.
"We're seeing a very low volume because many institutional investors are already on holiday and those who are not prefer to wait until next year to get active again," said one dealer.
He added that "the market remains very sluggish, there's low activity, and a quiet volume base".
Bel-20 shares were helped by last Friday's EU agreement on the stability pact, a mechanism for ensuring monetary discipline after the launch of a single currency in 1999.
Friday's flat close for the Dow Jones and its higher opening on Monday calmed nervous investors that the Dow was in for a major sell-off, helping the Brussels bourse.
But dealers said investors who were buying stocks before Christmas were now awaiting Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Commitee, which sets U.S. interest rates.
"Investors are certainly waiting for the FOMC meeting tomorrow," one dealer said.
But he added that volumes looked set to remain thin.
Another dealer said there was room for further slight rises before the new year if economic figures remained positive and neigbouring bourses performed well.
"But volume will be thin ahead of Christmas," he said.

Financials regained some lost ground after Friday's profit taking, with insurance group Fortis AG rising 2.21 percent to 4,855 francs. Fortis AG was also helped on by strong gains in its sister unit Fortis AMEV in Holland.
Elsewhere among financials GBL rose 1.48 percent to 4,120 francs.
Among cyclicals Petrofina gained 2.0 percent to 10,200 after last week's losses affected by Wall Street uncertainty and Iraqi oil reserves to come onto the market.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert rose 0.88 percent to 22,975 francs, with one dealer saying "Bekaert is still a good stock at this price to buy".
Bekaert said after the bourse closed that it expected 1996 current profits to be cut to near break-even following provisions for a structural improvement programme.
